The zero-margin README says that only N21PtsLower.lean, the axiom report and the build script are the author's; the root README says parts of the work were produced with AI assistance under human direction.
claims: point_n21_L5/lean/zero-margin/N21PtsLower.lean states theorem SquarePacking.n21pts_ge_5 : (5 : ℝ) ≤ minSide 21 and theorem SquarePacking.n21pts_eq_5 : minSide 21 = 5, with no hypothesis; the README reports '-- depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]' for n21pts_eq_5.

The certificate is point_n21_L5/certificates/n21-capture-one.txt (SHA-256 9f631fbae420e0376ea636a232b7680e937deebe205dc035cfb9c43a3d74b456), the point-only cover renormalised to capture threshold 1: 4,604 entries of [0,5]^2 with weights w/999948000000, total 20998900000168/999948000000 < 21.

The lower bound applies Evan Daniel's BoxTree.le_minSide to a zero-margin box tree generated by his gen_zmtree.py (untrusted, deterministic) at evand/square-packing 6aa82ba457e9eaeaaa3af0833600f27f91a2fce3: 59,433 Z leaves, 5,876 E leaves and 5,591 clips in 2,076 chunks over 64 files, each chunk decide +kernel of ZMTree.check (ZMTree.sound); the 5 x 5 grid (packs_grid) gives the equality. The 66 generated files (88 MB) are not in the tree; data-sha256.txt lists their SHA-256.

The source reports a run on an Apple M4 under load: generation 1,459 s wall on 6 workers, the kernel check about 3.5 h wall with 2 parts at a time, near 6 GB per part, and an end-to-end run of build_zero_margin.sh from an empty directory ending N21_POINTS_HYPOTHESIS_FREE_VERIFIED with the regenerated data matching data-sha256.txt. No build log is published.
